_comment: Cardinal number words and the quantity each names, for the counting-picture
production card (see app/cards/number_image.py and no/numbers.json, whose
rules this file follows). tunatale-w4m7.4, 2026-09-23.
Tagalog has TWO number systems in daily use, and the user's decision
(2026-09-23) is to learn both, each in the context Filipinos use it: native
for counting things and people, Spanish-derived for clock time and prices
(see data/style.md). A counting picture can carry only ONE production per
quantity (`values` must be injective after `exclude`), and counting objects is
the NATIVE context, so the native words get the picture.
`exclude`:
isa      — 'one' AND the indefinite 'a/an' (isang bata = a child); a picture
of one thing is equally 'a thing'. Same reasoning as Norwegian `en`.
sandaan  — a doublet of isandaan (100); isandaan is the produced form.
the Spanish-derived words — their context is a clock face or a price, not a
heap. ⚠️ An excluded word takes the ordinary card route, which can
fetch a PHOTO of a numeral. Spanish-number cards need their own
route (a clock face for alas-X, a peso amount); that is a follow-up
bead, not something this file can fix.
Every Spanish-derived cardinal is listed anyway, so this file records that
they were considered rather than overlooked, and so the follow-up has its
vocabulary. 0 and 1000 are listed for the same reason; the renderable range
lives only in number_image.py::MAX_RENDERABLE.
